_schema.purpose: Anchor patterns for bootstrap energy calibration when stored calibration fails the 0.3*FWHM residual test. Each pattern is a group of lines whose relative energy positions are invariant under any monotonic calibration.

fields.name: human-readable identifier
fields.lines: ordered list of line energies in keV (low to high)
fields.intensity_ratios: optional, expected intensity ratios I_i/I_0 (relative to first line)
fields.tolerance_keV: max allowed deviation of inter-line distance after fitted calibration
fields.context: when this pattern is reliable to look for
fields.single_line: true if pattern is a single isolated line (useful for offset/gain fix only, not curvature)

_schema.usage: Algorithm: for each pattern, find candidate channel-tuples whose spacing matches expected energy spacing (within tolerance). Fit linear/quadratic E(N) iteratively, prioritizing higher-priority patterns.

patterns.name: Natural background NaI ERN-line set
patterns.context: Lsrm-recommended reference line set for NaI energy calibration on natural-background (ЕРН) spectra. Seven lines spanning 240–2615 keV — robust shape constraint for polynomial fit up to degree 3. Two lines are superpositions that are unresolvable on NaI but whose energy uncertainty is negligible relative to the detector's FWHM: 240 keV = Pb-212 (239, Th-232 chain) + Pb-214 (242, Ra-226 chain); 511 keV = Tl-208 (510.77, Th-232 chain) + annihilation γ. The other five are clean single lines: Pb-214 351.93, Bi-214 1120.29, K-40 1460.82, Bi-214 1764.49, Tl-208 2614.51. Source: Lsrm Algorithmic Foundations, рекомендации по калибровке сцинтилляционных детекторов на ЕРН-спектрах. Intensity ratios deliberately omitted because activity composition varies between Th-dominated, Ra-dominated, and mixed natural-background spectra; use as energy anchor only.

patterns.name: Th-232 chain triplet
patterns.context: Pure Th-232 source or natural background dominated by Th chain (no Ra contamination). Three lines from three different daughters: Pb-212, Tl-208 (lower), Tl-208 (upper). Spans 240 keV to 2614 keV — excellent shape constraint for polynomial calibration.

patterns.name: K-40 + Tl-208 high-energy pair
patterns.context: Most reliable bootstrap seed for natural-background spectra: two clean isolated lines >1000 keV apart with no plausible interference. K-40 is always present from environment; Tl-208 is always present from Th-232 in concrete/soil.

patterns.name: Co-60 doublet
patterns.context: Calibration source. The ratio E2/E1 = 1.1357 is invariant — strongest anchor when Co-60 is present.

patterns.name: Tl-208 + Bi-214 natural-background quartet
patterns.context: Always-on natural background. Tl-208 2614 is the cleanest high-energy anchor available.

patterns.name: K-40 single
patterns.context: Universal natural background. Single line — can fix gain but not curvature alone.

patterns.name: Annihilation 511
patterns.context: Present whenever a positron emitter is in the sample or pair production occurs (parent γ > 1022 keV). Width is Doppler-broadened — match by center, not width. NOTE 1: epiphenomenon, not a primary anchor. Physically absent from pure-source spectra where every photopeak is ≤ 1022 keV (e.g. pure Cs-137 with photopeak at 661.66 keV cannot produce 511). NOTE 2: in spectra containing Th-232 chain (Tl-208), the 510.77 keV line of Tl-208 (I≈22.6%) is unresolvable on NaI from true 511 annihilation. The 511 ROI counts in such spectra are dominated by Tl-208 510.77 proportional to other Tl-208 lines, NOT by annihilation. For bootstrap calibration the 0.23 keV difference is negligible (FWHM at 500 keV on NaI 50×50 is ~30 keV); for identification it must be disambiguated by checking the Tl-208 583.19 and 2614.51 lines. Use only when corroborated by another anchor or when E > 1022 keV photopeaks are present.

patterns.name: Cs-137 single
patterns.context: Fallout / calibration source. Very distinctive when present.

patterns.name: Cs-137 + Ba Kα IC pair
patterns.context: Cs-137 is always accompanied by Ba Kα at 32.07 keV from internal conversion of the 661.66 line in the ¹³⁷ᵐBa daughter. Intensity ratio I(Ba Kα)/I(661.66) ≈ 0.066 — small but always detectable above any LLD that lets the 32 keV through. This wide pair gives an unambiguous low-E/high-E anchor for pure Cs-137 calibration sources where no other natural-background line is present. Note: Ba Kβ at 36 keV often visible too, but Kα is the cleaner anchor.

patterns.name: Cs-137 + K-40 + Tl-208 environmental triplet
patterns.context: Three widely-spaced isolated lines spanning 660–2615 keV, always co-present in post-Chernobyl food/soil samples from contaminated regions (Belarus, Ukraine, Bryansk, Altai). Cs-137 from fallout, K-40 from biological potassium, Tl-208 from soil-borne Th-232 chain in the sample matrix. Intensity ratios deliberately omitted because Cs-137 activity varies by sample. Use as energy anchor only, not intensity check.

patterns.name: Bi-214 multi-line
patterns.context: Natural background. Rich multi-line set — robust for polynomial fitting if at least 4 lines visible. WARNING: on NaI 50×50 with limited statistics, often only 3-4 of these 8 lines exceed the σ-threshold; in such cases `Ra-226 NaI core` (3 lines from Pb-214 + Bi-214) is the appropriate fallback.

patterns.name: Ra-226 NaI core
patterns.context: Three brightest, well-spaced lines of the Ra-226 decay chain that are reliably visible on NaI 50×50 spectra even with short exposures (Pb-214 352 keV from Bi-214 daughter; Bi-214 609 keV; Bi-214 1764 keV). Spans 350–1765 keV — excellent shape constraint for linear+quadratic polynomial calibration. Use instead of the 8-line `Bi-214 multi-line` when fewer peaks are found on low-resolution scintillators. WARNING: Bi-214 609 keV is unresolvable from Tl-208 583.19 on NaI; verify absence of Tl-208 2614 keV before assigning this pattern.

patterns.name: Pb-214 doublet
patterns.context: Natural background. Good mid-energy anchor for the 300-400 keV region.

patterns.name: Ac-228 triplet
patterns.context: Th-232 chain. Useful when Th-bearing samples or natural background is present.

patterns.name: Eu-152 calibration multi-line
patterns.context: Best multi-energy calibration source. Use whenever Eu-152 is present. TCS-affected at close geometry — flag if ratios fail.

patterns.name: Ba-133 calibration set
patterns.context: Low-energy calibration source. Useful for the 80-400 keV range.

patterns.name: Am-241 low-energy
patterns.context: Single low-energy line; useful for fixing the low-energy offset. WARNING: overlaps W Ka1 if W shielding present.

patterns.name: Pb K X-ray quartet
patterns.context: Pb shielding. Present in any Pb-shielded measurement above ~85 keV gamma flux. Excellent fine-scale anchor for low-energy region.

patterns.name: Na-22 511 + 1274
patterns.context: Common calibration source. The 511 broadening must be accounted for.
